content.title: About
content.content: Dried figs are the dehydrated fruits of the common fig tree (Ficus carica), cultivated in warm regions of the Mediterranean, the Middle East, and California. They have a sweet, slightly caramel-like flavor and a soft, chewy texture. Dried figs are often enjoyed as a snack, added to baked goods, muesli, salads, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: When stored in an airtight container in a cool, dry place, dried figs can keep for up to a year.
Fig cultivation dates back more than 6,000 years, with evidence from ancient Mesopotamia.
Because of their natural sugars, dried figs are frequently used as a natural sweetener.
In ancient Egypt, figs were a symbol of fertility and featured in religious rituals.
The fiber content of dried figs is higher than fresh figs due to moisture removal.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dried figs provide about 9 g of dietary fiber per 100 g, supporting healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: They contain potassium, magnesium, calcium, and iron, which are essential for muscle, nerve, and blood health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Figs are a good source of polyphenols such as resveratrol and quercetin, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Heart‑friendly
items.content: Potassium and fiber in figs may help lower blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.title: Natural source of sugars
items.content: The fructose and glucose in dried figs provide quick energy, useful for athletes and people with high energy needs.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Dried figs are rich in natural sugars, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Fig allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to figs, ranging from skin rash to swelling or breathing difficulties.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Figs contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Commercially packaged figs may contain added sugar or preservatives; always check the ingredient list.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried figs can be eaten straight as a snack, added to muesli, yogurt, oatmeal, baked goods, salads, or used in sauces and spreads. Soaking them in warm water can re‑hydrate them slightly for use in desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried figs in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent spoilage and flavor loss.
